stemBlocks.value: A rectangular field ABCD measures 60 m by 40 m. A vertical mast MT of height 18 m stands at the centre M, and a cable runs from the top T to each corner. a) Calculate the horizontal distance AM. b) Calculate the angle of elevation of T from A, to 1 decimal place. c) Calculate the length of cable AT. d) Hence determine the minimum total length of cable required for all four corners, allowing an additional 2% for fastening, to the nearest metre.
Think first: The centre of a rectangle is the midpoint of each diagonal, so AM is exactly half the diagonal.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p177-q03 from workbook page 177.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the diagonal of the field.

contentBlocks.value: M is the centre, so AM = AC ÷ 2 = 72.111 ÷ 2

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the angle of elevation of T from A.

contentBlocks.value: MT is vertical, so tan θ = 18 ÷ 36.0555 = 0.49923

solutionSteps.instruction: Total the four cables and add 2%.

strategyBlocks.value: Find the base diagonal and halve it for AM, use tangent for the elevation, use Pythagoras with the 18 m mast for AT, then multiply by four and add 2%.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) AM ≈ 36.1 m  (b) angle of elevation ≈ 26.5°  (c) AT ≈ 40.3 m  (d) total cable required ≈ 164 m

whyThisWorks.value: Because the mast stands at the centre and is perpendicular to the whole base, every corner is the same horizontal distance from M — half a diagonal — so all four cables are equal and only one needs calculating. The mast being vertical is what guarantees the right angle at M, letting Pythagoras carry a two-dimensional distance up into three dimensions. The 2% allowance is a multiplication by 1.02 applied after totalling.

commonErrors.misconception: Using 60 m or 40 m as AM instead of half the diagonal.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using 60 m or 40 m as AM instead of half the diagonal.

commonErrors.misconception: Calculating AT for one corner and forgetting to multiply by four.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Calculating AT for one corner and forgetting to multiply by four.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding 2 m instead of 2%, or applying the 2% to a single cable only.

examTip.value: In 3-D problems, identify the horizontal distance first and treat the vertical as a separate right-angled step — the two-stage approach keeps the working clear and the marks separate.
